name: Bergisel-Schanze
kurzbeschreibung: The Bergiselschanze in Innsbruck combines Olympic ski jumping history with futuristic architecture by Zaha Hadid and a 360-degree panoramic restaurant.
oeffnungszeiten: Sommer täglich 09:00–18:00 Uhr, Winter Mi–Mo 09:00–17:00 Uhr (Di Ruhetag)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Bergiselschanze on historic Bergisel in southern Innsbruck is an internationally renowned sporting venue and a striking architectural landmark of Tyrol. As the traditional third stop of the prestigious Four Hills Tournament (Vierschanzentournee), the large hill draws a worldwide sports audience every year in early January. Perched approximately 250 metres above the rooftops of the Tyrolean capital, the spectacular structure offers an unparalleled 360-degree panoramic view of the Inntal valley and the rugged limestone peaks of the Nordkette from its viewing platform and the Bergisel SKY panoramic restaurant.

History & Architecture

The first ski jumps at Bergisel took place as early as 1927 on a simple natural hill. The ski stadium achieved world renown by hosting two Olympic Winter Games in 1964 and 1976 ? the historic cauldron at the outrun commemorates the ceremonial lightings of the Olympic flame. It also hosted the Nordic World Ski Championships in 1985 and 2019, while Pope John Paul II celebrated Holy Mass here in 1988 before 60,000 faithful. In 2001 and 2002, the ski jump was completely rebuilt according to bold designs by world-renowned British-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid. The sculptural silhouette merges the inrun tower, inclined elevator, panoramic restaurant, and viewing terrace into a seamless flowing form, earning the Austrian State Prize for Architecture in 2002. The tower stands 47 metres high; the facility features a K-point of 120 metres and a hill size of 128 metres.

Visit & Getting There

The ski jump facility welcomes visitors during the summer season (June to October) daily from 09:00 to 18:00. In the winter season (November to May), it is open Wednesday to Monday from 09:00 to 17:00 (closed on Tuesdays). Admission rates (2025/2026 season): Adults ? 12.00, seniors ? 11.00, children aged 6 to 14 ? 6.50, children under 6 free. Admission is complimentary with the all-inclusive Innsbruck Card. The ticket price includes rides on the modern inclined elevator and both passenger lifts inside the tower. Getting there by public transport: Tram line 1 or the Stubaitalbahn (STB) to the Bergisel station, followed by an approx. 10-minute walk uphill; alternatively, the hop-on/hop-off Sightseer bus stops right at the entrance next to the Tirol Panorama. By car: A13 motorway (exit Innsbruck-S?d) or A12 (exit Innsbruck-Mitte); pay parking is available directly along Bergiselweg.

Tips

The entire complex is exemplary in its barrier-free design: Step-free pathways, an inclined elevator, and modern tower lifts offer wheelchair users and families with strollers unrestricted access to the tower and restaurant. From May to October, weather permitting, show training takes place almost daily, allowing visitors to watch elite ski jumpers launching off the table at close range. Book a window table in advance at the Bergisel SKY tower restaurant for an unforgettable breakfast above the clouds.
